pick.headline: Nicaragua shoots down a CIA-linked supply plane; Hasenfus captured
pick.summary: On 5 October 1986 Sandinista troops shot down a C-123 cargo plane carrying arms to the contras over southern Nicaragua. The sole survivor, the American Eugene Hasenfus, was captured.
pick.significance: Hasenfus's capture exposed the private supply network run from the White House by Oliver North, a month before the Iran arms sales were revealed; together they became the Iran-Contra affair.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Latin America, Vol. VI No. 195, 8 October 1986
evidence.snippet: …hand, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said that, so far, the military has not received any official report from the Nicaraguan Government concerning this case. Meanwhile, U.S. Embassy sources told AFP the American Euguene Hasenfus, who was captured in Nicaragua because he was travelling in the plane that was shot down, does not belong to the group of U.S. advisers stationed here "and has not had any connection with the embassy."

alternates.headline: Chileans vote No to Pinochet
alternates.summary: On 5 October 1988 Chileans voted in a plebiscite to reject another eight years of rule by General Augusto Pinochet.
alternates.significance: The vote opened Chile's transition to democracy and elections the following year.
